root_causes: Removing the defective read_vizier broke its only consumer, and no test covered that consumer, so the break was silent
JSON serialization was never asserted to be strict, so a permissive default was indistinguishable from a correct one
The flag span had been recorded as UNVERIFIED from an assumption rather than checked against the ReadMe
An early version of _split_parent_row stripped the whole line before splitting, collapsing leading empty fields and breaking VizieR units rows; caught by an existing test before commit

findings: A CI run per event type is not interchangeable: the same SHA d1082ce passed CI on push (40122701389) and failed on pull_request (40122728663), because the cumulative lifecycle gate only runs on pull_request and only requires a cycle record there. Neither result can stand in for the other
Removing a function from a script requires checking every consumer; scripts/ has no __init__.py and no coverage for diagnose_cpvs_selection.py, so imports are unverified by default
Python's json.dumps emits NaN and Infinity by default. An artifact can look fine to json.loads in Python and still be unparseable elsewhere, so strictness has to be asserted, not assumed
A documented range can disprove the applicability of a documented cut: Flag [0/4628] means catflags != 32768 is vacuous here, and offering it as a policy would have implied a test that can never fail
